args.reason: The old decision rested on an explicit premise (under 20 issues per run, simplicity) that the new decision shows no longer holds: runs now admit 200+ issues and the concurrency executor writes in parallel. The new design addresses two concrete failure modes (one-lock contention, a single corrupt byte losing the whole run) and keeps the same directory root plus an index for discovery. The supersession argument is sound. Residual risk for implementation, not grounds to overturn: per-issue writes and index updates must stay atomic so the index cannot drift from the per-issue files.
